sanskrit: svayaṃ kṛtvā tu yaḥ pāpaṃ śubham evānutiṣṭhati prāyaścittaṃ naraḥ kartum ubhayaṃ so 'śnute pṛthak
english: But the man who, having himself committed an evil deed, then sets himself to do good as an expiation for it — he reaps the fruit of both, each separately.

sanskrit: ajñānāt tu kṛtāṃ hiṃsām ahiṃsā vyapakarṣati brāhmaṇāḥ śāstranirdeśād ity āhur brahmavādinaḥ
english: Harm done through ignorance is drawn off and cancelled by harmlessness — so say the brāhmaṇas who expound the Veda, citing the direction of the scriptures.

sanskrit: tathā kāmakṛtaṃ cāsya vihiṃsaivāpakarṣati ity āhur dharmaśāstrajñā brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ
english: And harm done willfully, out of desire, is likewise drawn off only by the renunciation of harm — so declare the brāhmaṇas learned in the dharma-scriptures, who have crossed to the far shore of the Veda.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu tāvat paśyāmi karma yad vartate kṛtam guṇayuktaṃ prakāśaṃ ca pāpenānupasaṃhitam
english: For my part, I hold that the deed which yields its fruit is the one performed endowed with virtue, open and shining, and untainted by any evil.

sanskrit: yathā sūkṣmāṇi karmāṇi phalantīha yathātatham buddhiyuktāni tānīha kṛtāni manasā saha
english: Subtle deeds bear their fruit here in just measure, exactly as they are — those, that is, which are done with discernment and with the mind fully present.

sanskrit: bhavaty alpaphalaṃ karma sevitaṃ nityam ulbaṇam abuddhipūrvaṃ dharmajña kṛtam ugreṇa karmaṇā
english: But a deed, O knower of dharma, though pursued unceasingly and on a grand scale, bears scant fruit when done without forethought, by violent means.

sanskrit: kṛtāni yāni karmāṇi daivatair munibhis tathā nācaret tāni dharmātmā śrutvā cāpi na kutsayet
english: Those deeds that were done by gods and by sages — the righteous man should not himself perform them; yet, having heard of them, neither should he revile them.

sanskrit: saṃcintya manasā rājan viditvā śaktim ātmanaḥ karoti yaḥ śubhaṃ karma sa vai bhadrāṇi paśyati
english: He who, O king, having pondered in his mind and gauged his own strength, performs a good deed — he indeed comes to see blessings.

sanskrit: nave kapāle salilaṃ saṃnyastaṃ hīyate yathā navetare tathābhāvaṃ prāpnoti sukhabhāvitam
english: As water poured into a fresh, unfired vessel seeps away and is lost, so too does happiness, when set in an unprepared soul, come to nothing.

sanskrit: satoye 'nyat tu yat toyaṃ tasminn eva prasicyate vṛddhe vṛddhim avāpnoti salile salilaṃ yathā
english: But as water poured into water that is already there only swells what was full, growing greater in the abundant, so does merit added to merit increase.

sanskrit: evaṃ karmāṇi yānīha buddhiyuktāni bhūpate nasamānīha hīnāni tāni puṇyatamāny api
english: Thus, O lord of the earth, the deeds done here with discernment are not matched even by the holiest of deeds done without it.

sanskrit: rājñā jetavyāḥ sāyudhāś connatāś ca; samyak kartavyaṃ pālanaṃ ca prajānām agniś ceyo bahubhiś cāpi yajñair; ante madhye vā vanam āśritya stheyam
english: The king must conquer those who are armed and arrogant, and must rightly protect his subjects; he must tend the sacred fire and worship with many sacrifices; and at the end, or even at the middle of life, he should withdraw to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: damānvitaḥ puruṣo dharmaśīlo; bhūtāni cātmānam ivānupaśyet garīyasaḥ pūjayed ātmaśaktyā; satyena śīlena sukhaṃ narendra
english: A man possessed of self-restraint and of righteous character should regard all beings as he regards himself; he should honor his betters according to his power, and through truth and good conduct, O lord of men, he attains happiness.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca kaḥ kasya copakurute kaś ca kasmai prayacchati prāṇī karoty ayaṃ karma sarvam ātmārtham ātmanā
english: Parāśara said: Who renders service to whom, and who bestows anything upon another? This living being performs every deed by himself and for his own sake.

sanskrit: gauraveṇa parityaktaṃ niḥsnehaṃ parivarjayet sodaryaṃ bhrātaram api kim utānyaṃ pṛthagjanam
english: One who has cast off all respect and is devoid of affection should be shunned — even a brother born of the same womb, how much more some other, a stranger of the common crowd.

sanskrit: viśiṣṭasya viśiṣṭāc ca tulyau dānapratigrahau tayoḥ puṇyataraṃ dānaṃ tad dvijasya prayacchataḥ
english: For a worthy man, the giving and the receiving from another worthy man are of equal merit; yet of the two, the giving is the holier — that is, the gift of a twice-born man who bestows.

sanskrit: nyāyāgataṃ dhanaṃ varṇair nyāyenaiva vivardhitam saṃrakṣyaṃ yatnam āsthāya dharmārtham iti niścayaḥ
english: Wealth that has come by lawful means to the social orders, and lawfully increased, must be guarded with effort — this is the settled rule — for the sake of dharma.

sanskrit: na dharmārthī nṛśaṃsena karmaṇā dhanam arjayet śaktitaḥ sarvakāryāṇi kuryān narddhim anusmaret
english: One who seeks dharma should not earn wealth by cruel means; he should carry out all his undertakings according to his capacity, and should not hanker after riches.

sanskrit: apo hi prayataḥ śītās tāpitā jvalanena vā śaktito 'tithaye dattvā kṣudhārtāyāśnute phalam
english: For the man of self-control who, to the best of his means, gives a guest tormented by hunger so much as cool water, or water warmed by fire, reaps the fruit of it.

sanskrit: rantidevena lokeṣṭā siddhiḥ prāptā mahātmanā phalapatrair atho mūlair munīn arcitavān asau
english: By great-souled Rantideva the perfection longed for by all the worlds was attained, for he honored the sages with offerings of fruits, leaves, and roots.

sanskrit: tair eva phalapatraiś ca sa māṭharam atoṣayat tasmāl lebhe paraṃ sthānaṃ śaibyo 'pi pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: With those very fruits and leaves he gratified Māṭhara; and through that the lord of the earth Śaibya too gained the highest station.

sanskrit: devatātithibhṛtyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyo 'thātmanas tathā ṛṇavāñ jāyate martyas tasmād anṛṇatāṃ vrajet
english: A mortal is born a debtor to the gods, to guests, to dependents, to the ancestors, and likewise to his own self; therefore let him strive to be free of debt.

sanskrit: svādhyāyena maharṣibhyo devebhyo yajñakarmaṇā pitṛbhyaḥ śrāddhadānena nṛṇām abhyarcanena ca
english: To the great seers the debt is discharged by recitation of the Veda, to the gods by the rite of sacrifice, to the ancestors by the offering of the śrāddha, and to men by hospitable honoring.

sanskrit: vācaḥ śeṣāvahāryeṇa pālanenātmano 'pi ca yathāvad bhṛtyavargasya cikīrṣed dharmam āditaḥ
english: By offering of the remnant of one's words, and by the sustaining of one's own self and of the whole body of dependents in due measure — thus let a man set out to fulfill dharma from the very beginning.

sanskrit: prayatnena ca saṃsiddhā dhanair api vivarjitāḥ samyag ghutvā hutavahaṃ munayaḥ siddhim āgatāḥ
english: Sages, perfected through effort and bereft even of wealth, attained to perfection by rightly making oblation into the fire that bears the offerings.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya putratvam ṛcīkatanayo 'gamat ṛgbhiḥ stutvā mahābhāgo devān vai yajñabhāginaḥ
english: The son of Ṛcīka, that highly blessed one, came to the sonship of Viśvāmitra, having praised with hymns of the Ṛgveda the gods who partake of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: gataḥ śukratvam uśanā devadevaprasādanāt devīṃ stutvā tu gagane modate tejasā vṛtaḥ
english: Uśanas attained the state of the planet Śukra by propitiating the god of gods; having praised the goddess, he now rejoices in the sky, wreathed in his own splendor.

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva tathā nāradaparvatau kakṣīvāñ jāmadagnyaś ca rāmas tāṇḍyas tathāṃśumān
english: Asita Devala, and likewise Nārada and Parvata, Kakṣīvat, and Rāma the son of Jamadagni, Tāṇḍya, and Aṃśumat —

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho jamadagniś ca viśvāmitro 'trir eva ca bharadvājo hariśmaśruḥ kuṇḍadhāraḥ śrutaśravāḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha and Jamadagni, Viśvāmitra and Atri, Bharadvāja, Hariśmaśru, Kuṇḍadhāra, and Śrutaśravas —

sanskrit: ete maharṣayaḥ stutvā viṣṇum ṛgbhiḥ samāhitāḥ lebhire tapasā siddhiṃ prasādāt tasya dhīmataḥ
english: these great seers, with collected minds, having praised Viṣṇu with hymns of the Ṛgveda, won perfection through their austerity, by the grace of that wise lord.

sanskrit: anarhāś cārhatāṃ prāptāḥ santaḥ stutvā tam eva ha na tu vṛddhim ihānvicchet karma kṛtvā jugupsitam
english: Even the unworthy, by praising that very lord, became worthy; but one should not seek prosperity here by doing a deed that is to be despised.

sanskrit: ye 'rthā dharmeṇa te satyā ye 'dharmeṇa dhig astu tān dharmaṃ vai śāśvataṃ loke na jahyād dhanakāṅkṣayā
english: Those gains that come through dharma are real; those that come through unrighteousness — a curse upon them. One should never abandon the eternal dharma in the world out of craving for wealth.

sanskrit: āhitāgnir hi dharmātmā yaḥ sa puṇyakṛd uttamaḥ vedā hi sarve rājendra sthitās triṣv agniṣu prabho
english: The righteous man who has established the sacred fires is the foremost of doers of merit; for all the Vedas, O lord among kings, O sovereign, abide within the three fires.

sanskrit: sa cāpy agnyāhito vipraḥ kriyā yasya na hīyate śreyo hy anāhitāgnitvam agnihotraṃ na niṣkriyam
english: That brāhmaṇa who has established the fires, but whose rites lapse — better for him the state of not having established them at all; for the fire-oblation is no fire-oblation when it goes unperformed.

sanskrit: agnir ātmā ca mātā ca pitā janayitā tathā guruś ca naraśārdūla paricaryā yathātatham
english: The sacred fire, one's own self, mother, father the begetter, and the teacher, O tiger among men — these are to be tended with service, each in its due measure.

sanskrit: mānaṃ tyaktvā yo naro vṛddhasevī; vidvān klībaḥ paśyati prītiyogāt dākṣyeṇāhīno dharmayukto nadānto; loke 'smin vai pūjyate sadbhir āryaḥ
english: The man who has cast off pride and serves his elders, who though learned looks upon them with the meekness of one without power, out of pure affection — not lacking in diligence, yoked to dharma and self-restrained — such a noble one is honored in this world by the good.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca vṛttiḥ sakāśād varṇebhyas tribhyo hīnasya śobhanā prītyopanītā nirdiṣṭā dharmiṣṭhān kurute sadā
english: Parāśara said: The livelihood of the lowliest, drawn from the three higher orders, is honorable; offered with goodwill and prescribed by rule, it ever makes men most righteous.

sanskrit: vṛttiś cen nāsti śūdrasya pitṛpaitāmahī dhruvā na vṛttiṃ parato mārgec chuśrūṣāṃ tu prayojayet
english: If a śūdra has no fixed livelihood handed down from father and grandfather, he should not seek a calling from another, but should set himself to the service of others.

sanskrit: sadbhis tu saha saṃsargaḥ śobhate dharmadarśibhiḥ nityaṃ sarvāsv avasthāsu nāsadbhir iti me matiḥ
english: Fellowship with the good, who perceive dharma, is becoming at all times and in every condition; never fellowship with the wicked — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: yathodayagirau dravyaṃ saṃnikarṣeṇa dīpyate tathā satsaṃnikarṣeṇa hīnavarṇo 'pi dīpyate
english: As an object glows by its nearness to the mountain of sunrise, so even a man of low birth shines by nearness to the good.

sanskrit: yādṛśena hi varṇena bhāvyate śuklam ambaram tādṛśaṃ kurute rūpam etad evam avaihi me
english: With whatever hue a white cloth is steeped, just that color it takes on — understand the matter from me to be exactly so.

sanskrit: tasmād guṇeṣu rajyethā mā doṣeṣu kadā cana anityam iha martyānāṃ jīvitaṃ hi calācalam
english: Therefore take your delight in virtues, never in vices; for the life of mortals here is impermanent, ever shifting and unsteady.

sanskrit: sukhe vā yadi vā duḥkhe vartamāno vicakṣaṇaḥ yaś cinoti śubhāny eva sa bhadrāṇīha paśyati
english: The wise man who, whether placed in happiness or in sorrow, gathers up only good deeds — he comes to behold blessings here.

sanskrit: dharmād apetaṃ yat karma yady api syān mahāphalam na tat seveta medhāvī na tad dhitam ihocyate
english: A deed that has fallen away from dharma, though it might bring great reward, the man of insight should not pursue; it is not called wholesome here.

sanskrit: yo hṛtvā gosahasrāṇi nṛpo dadyād arakṣitā sa śabdamātraphalabhāg rājā bhavati taskaraḥ
english: A king who, failing to protect his people, plunders thousands of cattle only to give them away, reaps as his fruit no more than empty repute — such a king becomes a thief.

sanskrit: svayaṃbhūr asṛjac cāgre dhātāraṃ lokapūjitam dhātāsṛjat putram ekaṃ prajānāṃ dhāraṇe ratam
english: The Self-existent first created the Ordainer, honored by the worlds; and the Ordainer created a single son, devoted to the upholding of all creatures.

sanskrit: tam arcayitvā vaiśyas tu kuryād atyartham ṛddhimat rakṣitavyaṃ tu rājanyair upayojyaṃ dvijātibhiḥ
english: Having worshiped him, the vaiśya should make his wealth abound exceedingly; it is then to be protected by the men of royal blood and put to use by the twice-born.

sanskrit: ajihmair aśaṭhakrodhair havyakavyaprayoktṛbhiḥ śūdrair nirmārjanaṃ kāryam evaṃ dharmo na naśyati
english: By śūdras who are honest, free from guile and from anger, and who furnish the means for offerings to the gods and to the ancestors, the cleansing service should be done — thus dharma does not perish.

sanskrit: apranaṣṭe tato dharme bhavanti sukhitāḥ prajāḥ sukhena tāsāṃ rājendra modante divi devatāḥ
english: When dharma is thus kept from perishing, the people become happy; and by their happiness, O lord of kings, the gods rejoice in heaven.

sanskrit: tasmād yo rakṣati nṛpaḥ sa dharmeṇābhipūjyate adhīte cāpi yo vipro vaiśyo yaś cārjane rataḥ
english: Therefore the king who protects his people is honored through dharma; so too the brāhmaṇa who studies, the vaiśya who is intent on earning,

sanskrit: yaś ca śuśrūṣate śūdraḥ satataṃ niyatendriyaḥ ato 'nyathā manuṣyendra svadharmāt parihīyate
english: and the śūdra who renders service, constantly and with senses controlled. Acting otherwise than this, O lord of men, a man falls away from his own dharma.

sanskrit: prāṇasaṃtāpanirdiṣṭāḥ kākiṇyo 'pi mahāphalāḥ nyāyenopārjitā dattāḥ kim utānyāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Even a few small coins, wrung from one's own life's hardship, earned by lawful means and given away, bear great fruit — how much more so other sums by the thousand.

sanskrit: satkṛtya tu dvijātibhyo yo dadāti narādhipa yādṛśaṃ tādṛśaṃ nityam aśnāti phalam ūrjitam
english: He who, doing them honor, gives to the twice-born, O lord of men, ever reaps a mighty fruit, each according to the manner of his giving.

sanskrit: abhigamya dattaṃ tuṣṭyā yad dhanyam āhur abhiṣṭutam yācitena tu yad dattaṃ tad āhur madhyamaṃ budhāḥ
english: What is given gladly, the giver himself approaching the recipient, the wise call the most blessed and most praised; but what is given upon being asked, the learned call middling.

sanskrit: avajñayā dīyate yat tathaivāśraddhayāpi ca tad āhur adhamaṃ dānaṃ munayaḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: What is given with contempt, and likewise without faith, that the truth-speaking sages call the lowest of gifts.

sanskrit: atikrame majjamāno vividhena naraḥ sadā tathā prayatnaṃ kurvīta yathā mucyeta saṃśayāt
english: A man, ever sinking in transgression of many kinds, should so exert himself that he may be delivered from the peril.

sanskrit: damena śobhate vipraḥ kṣatriyo vijayena tu dhanena vaiśyaḥ śūdras tu nityaṃ dākṣyeṇa śobhate
english: The brāhmaṇa shines by self-restraint, the kṣatriya by victory, the vaiśya by wealth, and the śūdra ever shines by diligence.

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca pratigrahāgatā vipre kṣatriye śastranirjitāḥ vaiśye nyāyārjitāś caiva śūdre śuśrūṣayārjitāḥ svalpāpy arthāḥ praśasyante dharmasyārthe mahāphalāḥ
english: Parāśara said: Goods that come to the brāhmaṇa through acceptance of gifts, to the kṣatriya as won by the sword, to the vaiśya as earned by lawful means, and to the śūdra as gained by service — even when slight, such goods are praised, and bear great fruit when used for the sake of dharma.

sanskrit: nityaṃ trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ śūdraḥ śuśrūṣur ucyate kṣatradharmā vaiśyadharmā nāvṛttiḥ patati dvijaḥ śūdrakarmā yadā tu syāt tadā patati vai dvijaḥ
english: The śūdra is declared the perpetual servant of the three orders. A twice-born man who follows the duty of a kṣatriya or of a vaiśya, when no other livelihood remains, does not fall; but when he takes up the work of a śūdra, then indeed the twice-born man falls.

sanskrit: vāṇijyaṃ pāśupālyaṃ ca tathā śilpopajīvanam śūdrasyāpi vidhīyante yadā vṛttir na jāyate
english: Trade, the keeping of cattle, and a living gained by craftsmanship are ordained even for the śūdra, when no other livelihood arises for him.

sanskrit: raṅgāvataraṇaṃ caiva tathā rūpopajīvanam madyamāṃsopajīvyaṃ ca vikrayo lohacarmaṇoḥ
english: Taking to the stage, a living gained by one's looks, subsisting upon liquor and meat, and the sale of iron and of leather —

sanskrit: apūrviṇā na kartavyaṃ karma loke vigarhitam kṛtapūrviṇas tu tyajato mahān dharma iti śrutiḥ
english: a deed the world reviles should not be taken up by one who has not done it before; but for one who has done it before and now forsakes it, there is great dharma — so says the sacred tradition.

sanskrit: saṃsiddhaḥ puruṣo loke yad ācarati pāpakam madenābhiplutamanās tac ca nagrāhyam ucyate
english: Whatever evil a man, however accomplished, commits in the world with a mind flooded by intoxicating pride — that too is declared not to be taken as a precedent.

sanskrit: śrūyante hi purāṇe vai prajā dhigdaṇḍaśāsanāḥ dāntā dharmapradhānāś ca nyāyadharmānuvartakāḥ
english: For in the lore of old we hear of peoples who were governed by the rod of reproach alone — self-restrained, holding dharma foremost, and following the path of justice and right.

sanskrit: dharma eva sadā nṝṇām iha rājan praśasyate dharmavṛddhā guṇān eva sevante hi narā bhuvi
english: It is dharma alone, O king, that is ever praised among men here; for men who have grown great in dharma cultivate the virtues upon the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ dharmam asurās tāta nāmṛṣyanta janādhipa vivardhamānāḥ kramaśas tatra te 'nvāviśan prajāḥ
english: That dharma, my son, the asuras could not endure, O lord of peoples; growing ever stronger, step by step they entered into those creatures.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ darpaḥ samabhavat prajānāṃ dharmanāśanaḥ darpātmanāṃ tataḥ krodhaḥ punas teṣām ajāyata
english: Then arrogance, the destroyer of dharma, arose in those creatures; and out of their arrogance, wrath in turn was born within them.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhābhibhūtānāṃ vṛttaṃ lajjāsamanvitam hrīś caivāpy anaśad rājaṃs tato moho vyajāyata
english: Then, in those overpowered by wrath, all conduct accompanied by decency perished, and modesty itself perished, O king; and from this delusion was born.

sanskrit: tato mohaparītās te nāpaśyanta yathā purā parasparāv amardena vartayanti yathāsukham
english: Then, beset by delusion, they no longer saw, as before, how they might live with one another at ease, without crushing each the other.

sanskrit: tān prāpya tu sa dhig daṇḍo nakāraṇam ato 'bhavat tato 'bhyagacchan devāṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś cāvamanya ha
english: When that rod of mere reproach reached such men, it became of no avail against them; and so they went on to despise both the gods and the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu devā devavaraṃ śivam agacchañ śaraṇaṃ vīraṃ bahurūpaṃ gaṇādhipam
english: At this very time the gods went for refuge to Śiva, foremost of the gods, the hero of many forms, the lord of the hosts.

sanskrit: tena sma te gaganagāḥ sapurāḥ pātitāḥ kṣitau tisro 'py ekena bāṇena devāpyāyitatejasā
english: By him those sky-dwellers, together with their cities — all three — were cast down to the earth with a single arrow, whose splendor the gods had swelled.

sanskrit: teṣām adhipatis tv āsīd bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ devatānāṃ bhayakaraḥ sa hataḥ śūlapāṇinā
english: Their overlord was the dreadful Bhīma of dreadful prowess, a terror to the gods; he was slain by the Bearer of the Trident.

sanskrit: tasmin hate 'tha svaṃ bhāvaṃ pratyapadyanta mānavāḥ prāvartanta ca vedā vai śāstrāṇi ca yathā purā
english: When he was slain, men returned to their own true nature, and the Vedas and the scriptures were set going once more, as in the days of old.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyaṣiñcan rājyena devānāṃ divi vāsavam saptarṣayaś cānvayuñjan narāṇāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇe
english: Then they consecrated Vāsava to the kingship of the gods in heaven, and the Seven Seers appointed men to the wielding of the rod of chastisement.

sanskrit: saptarṣīṇām athordhvaṃ ca vipṛthur nāma pārthivaḥ rājānaḥ kṣatriyāś caiva maṇḍaleṣu pṛthak pṛthak
english: After the Seven Seers there was a king named Vipṛthu, and kings and kṣatriyas each ruling separately in their several realms.

sanskrit: mahākuleṣu ye jātā vṛttāḥ pūrvatarāś ca ye teṣām athāsuro bhāvo hṛdayān nāpasarpati
english: In those born of great lineages, and in those who lived in former ages, the asura nature does not slip away from the heart.

sanskrit: tasmāt tenaiva bhāvena sānuṣaṅgena pārthivāḥ āsurāṇy eva karmāṇi nyaṣevan bhīmavikramāḥ
english: Therefore, through that very nature clinging persistently to them, kings of dreadful might took to performing asura-like deeds.

sanskrit: pratyatiṣṭhaṃś ca teṣv eva tāny eva sthāpayanti ca bhajante tāni cādyāpi ye bāliśatamā narāḥ
english: They held firm to those very deeds and continue to establish them; and even to this day those men who are most foolish cling to them.

sanskrit: tasmād ahaṃ bravīmi tvāṃ rājan saṃcintya śāstrataḥ saṃsiddhādhigamaṃ kuryāt karma hiṃsātmakaṃ tyajet
english: Therefore I tell you, O king, after pondering it in the light of the scriptures: one should pursue what leads to true perfection, and forsake every deed whose essence is harm.
